# Optional connectors: Terraform (HashiCorp)

These MCP servers need a connection target (cluster endpoint, host, credentials, or a local runtime such as Docker) that only you can supply, so the plugin does **not** start them. Add the ones you need to your own agent host configuration with the exact key shown; the key determines the tool names (`mcp__<key>__*`).

Each connector below has a Claude Code command, a Codex command, and the equivalent `~/.codex/config.toml` block. Other MCP hosts take the same `command`, `args`, and `env`.

AWS credentials are inherited from your environment. Prefer least-privilege, read-only database users and keep write flags off unless you need them. Codex starts MCP servers with a minimal environment; if a server can't find your AWS profile, add `AWS_PROFILE` and `AWS_REGION` to its `env`.

## Connectors

| Key | Server | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `terraform` | [`hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server`](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server) | Live Terraform Registry lookups: provider resource/data-source docs, module search and inputs, and Sentinel/policy libraries. |

### `terraform`

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user terraform -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server
```

Codex:

```bash
codex mcp add terraform -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server
```

Codex `config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.terraform]
command = "docker"
args = ["run", "-i", "--rm", "hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server"]
```

Needs Docker (or swap in the release binary: `terraform-mcp-server stdio`). Without `TFE_TOKEN` it exposes only public-registry lookups, which is all the agent needs. Do not add `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS=true`: the agent runs `terraform plan`/`apply` itself so every change goes through the approval gate.
